steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: acceptance is not delivery
steps.detail: InternalNotificationController receives work at /internal/v1/notifications, checks the configured internal key and returns an accepted response after delegating to NotificationService.create. HTTP 202 means the request was accepted under that contract; it does not prove an email arrived or a device displayed a push. Follow the request record into inbox/channel handling and the delivery repository. Distinguish the originating business event, notification request, selected channel, individual provider attempt and eventual delivery evidence. A notification is normally a consequence of an Order, payment or subscription fact; Notification must not become the owner of that business transition merely because it sends the message.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: missing message versus missing business fact
steps.detail: When a customer reports no message, first determine whether the originating event exists, whether Notification accepted it, whether channel policy permitted delivery and whether a provider attempt has evidence. An in-app record, an accepted email API call and a recipient opening a message are different observations. A provider timeout does not necessarily mean nothing was sent. Do not repeat a payment, order or delivery action in order to regenerate its notification. Keep recipient identity and destination ownership separate from arbitrary request strings, and never include raw customer payloads or channel credentials in classroom logs.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: map a message into evidence stages
steps.detail: Read NotificationServiceInboxTest and NotificationServiceChannelPolicyTest, then run mvn -B -ntp -f services/notification-service/pom.xml -Dtest=NotificationServiceInboxTest,NotificationServiceChannelPolicyTest test. Create a synthetic order-status event and trace request acceptance, in-app visibility, channel eligibility, dispatch attempt and delivery evidence. For each stage, list the owning component and what a missing record would mean. Add one local negative fixture around the existing channel policy rather than enabling a provider. Deliver an evidence-stage table with an explicit statement of what HTTP 202 does and does not prove.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: an event-to-channel sequence, test output and a correct distinction between accepted, attempted and observed delivered/read states. No email, SMS, push or business event is sent to real recipients.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: use stable request identity for recovery
steps.detail: Trace how NotificationService and its repositories identify repeated work. A retry should refer to the same logical business event/request where the implemented contract requires it; changing the identifier on every attempt can create duplicate messages. Identify the durable request, attempt status and any provider reference before changing retry behavior. Read recovery authorization separately from customer inbox access. An administrator who can investigate a delivery problem does not automatically have permission to resend every channel or view every destination. Use the existing operational reason and audit contracts wherever the actual recovery endpoint requires them.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: classify the reason before retrying
steps.detail: A disabled channel, invalid destination, temporary provider outage, rate limit and unknown send outcome need different responses. Respect customer preferences and existing capability flags rather than treating them as transient errors to bypass. A permanent rejection should not enter an unbounded retry loop. An unknown provider result may need reconciliation before another send. For a support ticket, preserve safe request/event/provider references and timestamps, but redact addresses, device tokens, signed URLs and message bodies containing personal information. Do not claim the user read the message based solely on a provider acceptance response.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: rehearse five recovery decisions
steps.detail: Build five synthetic delivery records representing disabled, invalid, temporary, rate-limited and uncertain outcomes. For each, state retry, reconcile, correct through an approved path or stop, and identify the code/contract supporting that decision. Read NotificationDeliveryRepositoryTest for the actual persistence and recovery expectations; do not infer them from the class name. Run only its documented local test setup after inspection. Add a mock assertion that a repeated logical request cannot enqueue an extra send when the existing deduplication path says it is already handled. No live provider credentials or real customer destination should be present.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a recovery decision table, stable-identity explanation and a duplicate-send regression. The reviewer must be able to see why a missing notification does not justify replaying the underlying financial or fulfillment action.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: trace devices, preferences and documents
steps.detail: NotificationDeliveryController exposes device registration/list/deactivation and channel preferences under /api/v1/notifications. It derives identity from a verified CravesPrincipal, normalizes the platform and channel values and validates supported values in the controller. The reviewed platform list is ANDROID and IOS; the inspected preference boundary lists IN_APP, PUSH and EMAIL. Do not assume that this particular endpoint configures every possible communication channel elsewhere in the service. Follow identity-scoped repository calls and the response model. For PDF generation, read the documents module: business source services provide authorized saved facts, while Notification renders/stores/delivers the document. Rendering a receipt must not invent invoice tax treatment or recalculate a historical order from current prices.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: content, authorization and storage are separate
steps.detail: A generated PDF can be well formatted and still contain another customer's data. Verify authorization at document creation, source retrieval and download, then inspect the data snapshot used by the renderer. Private blob names or signed storage URLs should not be exposed without the approved access contract. Emailing a generated document is a separate controlled action from producing bytes. A renderer failure must not change Order's business state or erase financial source records. Do not claim email/PDF production readiness from a layout test alone; delivery and authenticated download require their own evidence.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: follow a synthetic document end to end
steps.detail: Read DocumentControllerTest and DocumentPdfRendererTest. Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/notification-service/pom.xml -Dtest=DocumentControllerTest,DocumentPdfRendererTest test after confirming the fixtures remain isolated. Trace authorized request, source lookup, saved amounts, brand/rendering, storage reference and download/email boundary. Include cases for wrong owner, missing source data, rendering failure and delivery disabled according to the tested contracts. Inspect the generated test document where the suite provides one, checking text wrapping and page breaks as well as values. Do not upload a real invoice or send a test email to a customer as part of the classroom lab.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a document data/permission lineage map and separate assertions for correctness, privacy and rendering. Label real authenticated download and email delivery unverified when only local tests were run.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: add a notification type without moving domain logic
steps.detail: Training-only feature brief: implement a synthetic in-app notification for completion of a fictional training task. Use the existing notification request/domain model in a local branch, not a direct mail-provider call from another service. Define a stable event/request identity, allowed payload keys, target verified identity, template data and channel behavior. Keep the payload minimal and free of credentials or customer order data. Decide which service owns the fictional event and why Notification only records/presents it. The task must not modify real Order, payment or delivery behavior, and its type must not be enabled in production configuration.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: template input is untrusted data
steps.detail: Bound text and reject unsupported payload fields according to the training contract. Do not render arbitrary HTML, execute template expressions from a request or copy raw exceptions into the message. Test duplicate event, disabled channel, missing required payload, wrong identity and malformed destination where applicable. Ensure a display-oriented notification cannot trigger another business operation on read. Keep customer preferences and feature flags effective. A new notification type needs an explicit compatibility strategy for older clients encountering an unknown type; a safe generic presentation may be appropriate, but silently treating it as a payment-success message is not.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: build a local in-app-only vertical slice
steps.detail: Create training/in-app-training-notice. Implement the fictional type against local mocks or the documented disposable test database. Write tests that one logical event produces one request and that retries do not duplicate the in-app record. Add a client parser and unknown-type/empty/error presentation tests. Assert no external channel adapter is invoked. Run NotificationServiceInboxTest, NotificationServiceChannelPolicyTest and the new tests, then the selected client's typecheck. Deliver the full file tree, complete changed files, synthetic request/response examples, deduplication proof and rollback plan. No actual messages, provider calls or production events are allowed.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: the complete local in-app feature, duplicate-event and privacy tests, and a no-external-send assertion. A reviewer should be able to remove the training type without changing the originating domain's state model.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: release record creation and sending separately
steps.detail: A notification module can store in-app work while an external channel remains disabled. Preserve that distinction in tests and activation plans. Review schema migrations, channel/provider bindings, identity scopes, templates, retry policy and document source contracts independently. Record the immutable source and artifact, previous healthy Notification revision and current configuration fingerprints before an actual release. Do not enable email, push, SMS or document delivery merely because code compiled. Academy course publication is not a Notification deployment and must not change its existing one-replica settings, worker flags or secret references.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: recover without rewriting source transactions
steps.detail: For missing or duplicate messages, find the source event, request identity, channel decision, attempt history and provider evidence before replay. For a bad PDF, preserve its source snapshot and diagnose whether the problem is authorization, business data, rendering or transport. A layout fix does not justify recalculating the receipt's amounts. Stop if a wrong owner receives a document or a retry creates unintended external sends. Contain the narrow channel or capability through the approved process, keep audit evidence and roll back compatible code where appropriate. Do not delete customer orders, payments or notification history as a shortcut.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: assemble a communication release gate
steps.detail: Run the selected inbox, channel-policy, controller and renderer tests locally. Build expected/actual/pass-fail rows for owner isolation, duplicate event, malformed payload, disabled delivery, renderer failure, unknown client type and safe recovery. Add a mock production checklist with source/image identity, migration status, prior revision, no-store/authorization checks and one-replica/configuration preservation. Mark actual email arrival, push display and authenticated document download pending unless independently observed. Simulate a channel outage and identify the smallest safe repair. The exercise must not send a message, change provider credentials or replay a real customer event.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: test output and a release/recovery packet that separates document bytes, in-app records and external delivery. Course completion does not grant authority to send messages or disclose private documents.
